requirements.title: Who may land and what a land request may carry
requirements.rationale: Landing writes to the target branch, yet an org member must be able to land their own change from a fork; the entry checks decide this before any attempt exists (LAND-FR-001, LAND-FR-003).

criteria.condition: a PAT without `changes:write` calls the land route, or a PAT without `changes:read` calls one of the three land read routes
criteria.action: refuse the request before looking up the workspace or the change
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`, the same for an existing and an unknown workspace; no land attempt is created

setup: a hub test fixture: a real store in t.TempDir(), a bare repository created with git init whose branch main holds one commit, a ready workspace `api` owned by user `owner`, and the land routes mounted on the real server pipeline with stub authentication

criteria.condition: an authenticated caller with the scope `changes:write` (or a credential without scopes) calls `POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/land`
criteria.action: admit the caller when the caller has write access to the target workspace, or when the caller's user is the author of the change and the workspace setting `land.by_author` is true, and refuse every other caller
criteria.contract: owner, admin token and the authoring member under `land.by_author: true` proceed to the preconditions; a member who is not the author, or the author under `land.by_author: false`, gets HTTP 403 `forbidden`; a caller with no read access gets HTTP 404 `not_found`; a refused call creates no land attempt

requirements.title: Preconditions and the land attempt record
requirements.rationale: A caller must learn at once why a land cannot start, and every land that does start must leave a durable record a caller can poll (LAND-FR-010, §8.3.2).

criteria.condition: a land request passes the entry checks and the preconditions
criteria.action: create a durable land attempt with status `running` before any replay starts, and keep every field of the attempt object present in every answer
criteria.contract: the attempt has `id` (UUID), `workspace_slug`, `target_branch`, `changes` (bottom first), `status` `running`, `trigger` `manual`, `strategy` equal to the workspace setting `land.strategy` at that moment, `attempts` 0, `noop` false, `commits` [], `requested_by` `{actor_type, actor_id, username}` of the caller, `session_id` as given or null, `created_at`, and null `onto_sha`, `landed_sha`, `conflict`, `blocked`, `error`, `override`, `finished_at`; `GET …/lands/:id` returns it

criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `change_not_open`; no land attempt is created and the target does not move

requirements.title: The policy gate
requirements.rationale: Nothing lands past policy, but policy is another package's; landing asks one gate once per change and obeys its answer (LAND-FR-011).

criteria.condition: a worker starts a `running` land attempt
criteria.action: ask the registered policy gate exactly once for each change of the attempt, bottom first, passing the workspace, the change, the version being landed and the caller; for an answer that is not `ready` on a request that carries `override`, ask the registered override rule whether the override lets that answer pass; proceed to the replay only when every answer is `ready` or passed
criteria.contract: with no gate registered the default gate answers `ready` with policy revision 0; with no override rule registered no override is applied; the attempt records the `policy_revision` the gate reported; neither the gate nor the rule is asked again when the compare-and-swap is retried

setup: an engine fixture: a real store and a bare repository in t.TempDir(), a workspace `api` with branch main, the default gate, and a helper that opens a change from a branch with given commits
check.pseudocode: in internal/land/gate_test.go with a recording gate: run an attempt for one change with override {reason: 'r'} while a second writer moves main once so that the compare-and-swap is retried: assert gate.calls == 1 and the call carried slug 'api', the change number, its current version and the caller; a recording override rule registered beside it was not asked, because the gate answered ready; assert the attempt ended landed with attempts == 2 and policy_revision == the revision the gate returned (7); then with no gate and no override rule registered run an attempt: assert it ended landed with policy_revision == 0 and override == null even though the request carried an override; then with a gate that answers pending and no override rule: assert the attempt ended blocked although the request carried an override

criteria.condition: the gate answers `pending` or `blocked` for a change of the attempt
criteria.action: end the attempt `blocked` without replaying or moving anything
criteria.contract: the attempt is final with `status` `blocked` and `blocked` = `{change, status, requirements[]}` of the first change, bottom first, that was not `ready`; the HTTP answer is 409 with `error_type` `policy_blocked` and the land attempt in `error.details`; the target does not move and the change stays `open`; one `parley.change.land_fail` event is written

criteria.action: record `override` on the attempt as `{reason}` with the reason of the request
criteria.contract: the final land attempt and the `parley.change.land` event metadata carry `override` = `{reason}`; when every change was `ready` without the rule, or the rule passed none, both carry null

requirements.title: Replay of the change onto the target head
requirements.rationale: The server does the rebase so that no client needs a clone, and a commit that does not apply must come back as data, not as a half-moved branch (LAND-FR-012, LAND-FR-013).

criteria.condition: an attempt with strategy `rebase` replays a change whose version does not sit directly on the target head
criteria.action: replay each of the change's own commits in order onto the target head, keeping each commit's author, author date and message and setting the committer to the landing identity of `[land].committer_name` and `[land].committer_email`
criteria.contract: the new target history is the target head followed by one new commit per own commit, in order; `commits` holds one `{change, version_sha, landed_sha}` per landed commit and `landed_sha` is the last one; the default committer is `Parley <parley@localhost>`

criteria.condition: an attempt with strategy `rebase` replays a change whose first own commit has the target head as its parent
criteria.action: use the change's commits as they are, without creating any commit
criteria.contract: the target moves to the version's head commit itself; every `commits` entry has `landed_sha` equal to `version_sha`

criteria.condition: an attempt with strategy `squash` replays a change
criteria.action: create one commit per change whose tree is the result of replaying the change's own commits onto the target head, whose author is the author of the version's head commit, and whose message is the change title, a blank line, the intent, a blank line and the trailers
criteria.contract: the trailers are `Parley-Change: <slug>#<number>`, then `Parley-Session: <id>` only when the change has a session, then one `Co-authored-by: Name <email>` per distinct author of the change's own commits other than the head commit's author; `commits` has one entry for the change with `version_sha` the version's head

requirements.title: Compare-and-swap with retry and atomic bookkeeping
requirements.rationale: Without a queue, the compare-and-swap is the only thing that keeps two lands from overwriting each other, and the bookkeeping must never disagree with the ref (LAND-FR-014, LAND-FR-015, LAND-FR-021).

criteria.condition: the target head is no longer the head the replay was built on when the compare-and-swap is tried
criteria.action: read the new target head, replay the change again onto it and try the compare-and-swap again, counting the try in `attempts`
criteria.contract: the attempt ends `landed` with `attempts` equal to the number of compare-and-swap tries (2 after one lost race) and `onto_sha` equal to the head the successful try was built on; its commits sit on top of the commits that moved the target
